page: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a high-density compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The hardware configuration features custom 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processors built on x86_64 architecture, providing 192 vCPUs across 96 dedicated physical cores. It includes 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no local storage disks and zero discrete GPUs, relying on network-attached storage architectures supported by a 50 Gbps baseline networking interface.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core computing capability, with stress-ng multi-core testing reaching 169,731.29 and PassMark CPU scores achieving 123,408.48. In single-core execution, Geekbench registered a strong score of 2,055.0. Hardware acceleration extensions including Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 (bf16 and vnni) deliver notable efficiency in matrix mathematical tasks and cryptography operations, reflected in top-tier results in PassMark encryption (177,655.82) and ray tracing (138,795.0).

Memory bandwidth testing highlights top-tier performance on small cached blocks at 13,859.76 GB/sec, with large block uncached read bandwidth reaching 419.18 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance recorded top-tier results in Redis operations with 176.17 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 115.71 GB/sec. CPU-driven inference tests on medium and large language models maintained solid prompt processing and token generation rates without dedicated GPU silicon.

A primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O operations must traverse the network fabric alongside standard data traffic. Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is functionally suited for distributed software compilation, large-scale batch compute workloads, CPU-based machine learning inference, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-cached key-value stores.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by the Nitro hypervisor and 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Utilizing x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores paired with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, reflecting a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-threaded processor performance, high-speed cached memory bandwidth, and elevated throughput in web serving and Redis key-value workloads. Integrated Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions enable efficient hardware-accelerated vector and matrix calculations. Without bundled local disk volumes, persistent storage requires network attachment. The instance is designed for large-scale code compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, compute-heavy simulation tasks, and high-concurrency web backend infrastructure.
